title: length, length(), size()
prompt: Which is correct for an `int[] a`?
explanation: Arrays: `.length` (field). Strings: `.length()` (method). Collections: `.size()`. Mixing these up is a rite of passage — get it over with now.

title: Largest element
prompt: Return the largest value in `nums` (always non-empty). Track a running max starting at `nums[0]`.

tests.note: all negative — don't start max at 0!

solution.explanation: Seeding with `nums[0]` (not 0) handles all-negative arrays — a classic hidden-test trap.

title: Reference semantics
prompt: After `int[] a = {1, 2}; int[] b = a; b[0] = 9;` — what is `a[0]`?
options: `9` — a and b point at the same array
explanation: Assignment copies the reference, not the data. For an independent copy: `int[] b = Arrays.copyOf(a, a.length);`

title: Count in a grid
prompt: Return how many cells in `grid` equal `target`. Nested loops over rows and columns.

solution.explanation: `grid.length` is the row count; `grid[0].length` is the column count.

hints: Outer loop `r` over `grid.length`, inner loop `c` over `grid[0].length`.

title: Drill: array sum
prompt: From memory: return the sum of all elements using an enhanced for loop (`for (int x : nums)`).

title: Drill: reverse in place
prompt: From memory: reverse `nums` in place using the two-pointer swap — `l` from the front, `r` from the back, swap and move inward while `l < r`. The method returns nothing; the grader checks the mutated array.

solution.explanation: The three-line swap with a temp variable is pure muscle memory — you'll write it hundreds of times.

hints: Swap needs a temp: `int t = nums[l]; nums[l] = nums[r]; nums[r] = t;`

title: Recall: create & fill
prompt: Fill in the array creation, fill, and length operations.
code:
int[] a = new int[{{1}}];     // n zero-filled slots
Arrays.{{2}}(a, -1);           // set every slot to -1
int len = a.{{3}};             // number of slots (no parentheses!)
explanation: `new int[n]` allocates n zeros, `Arrays.fill` overwrites them, and `.length` is a field (no parentheses).

title: Drill: build a filled array
prompt: From memory: return a new `int[]` of length `n` with every element equal to `val`.

title: Recall: sort & copy
prompt: Fill in the sort and sub-range copy operations.
code:
Arrays.{{1}}(a);                       // ascending, in place
int[] sub = Arrays.{{2}}(a, 1, 4);     // copy indices [1, 4)
explanation: `Arrays.sort` sorts in place; `Arrays.copyOfRange(a, from, to)` copies the half-open range [from, to).

title: Drill: sort ascending
prompt: From memory: sort `nums` ascending in place and return it (one `Arrays.sort` call).
